active_chat_goal: Act as the main responsible worker for AI-Statistician. Drive the hard central AgentRuntime and evaluation work toward blind, method-unspecified statistical discovery: generate competing theory/procedure candidates for unseen questions, derive them rigorously, implement and stress-test them in Python/R, freeze claim/theorem DAGs, and use Statlib/StatInference RAG plus real Lean feedback for progressive kernel closure. Preserve the strict reproduction/formalization benchmark and evidence boundaries, coordinate the canonical GitHub stream directly, and treat contracts and audits as enabling infrastructure rather than the product. The immediate gate is fresh exact-Haiku integrated consumption of preflight -> implementation -> independent review -> result-blind metric freeze -> confirmatory simulation, followed by whole-target RAG + Lean compiler-feedback closure. Fix only shared ACI, context, artifact-lineage, or runtime-transition defects exposed by traces; simplify or delete redundant scaffolding before adding components. Never add task answers, theorem-family rules, Lean grammar recipes, or tactic templates to runtime code.
main_objective: The primary product success criterion is blind, method-unspecified statistical discovery: from a previously unseen question or paper, LLM agents must propose competing methods, derive them rigorously, implement and stress-test them in Python/R, freeze a candidate theorem DAG, and use Statlib/StatInference RAG plus real Lean feedback to prove central claims or expose exact gaps. Reproduction/formalization is a distinct lane whose endpoint is an exact source theorem; novel discovery freezes and proves the system-authored candidate theorem instead. The default prover strategy is a general whole-target LLM coding agent with task-bound RAG and native Lean edit/check feedback; learned tactic-state policies or search trees are optional providers to evaluate, not a mandatory fixed proof strategy. Deterministic code owns execution, budgets, immutable lineage, validation, and evidence boundaries, not mathematical choices. Only active-project Lean/kernel verification proves a theorem.
